steps.body: In a right triangle, name the two short sides (the **legs**) a and b, and the long side opposite the right angle (the **hypotenuse**) c. The **Pythagorean theorem** says a² + b² = c². Build a square on each side to see why.

widget.prompt: Why does a² + b² = c²? Look at the squares on a 3-4-5 triangle.

panels.title: Leg squares
panels.body: The square on the leg of length 3 has area 9; the square on the leg of length 4 has area 16.

panels.title: Add them
panels.body: Together the two leg-squares cover 9 + 16 = 25 units of area.

panels.title: Hypotenuse square
panels.body: The square on the hypotenuse (length 5) has area 25 — exactly the combined leg-squares. So a² + b² = c².

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — the two leg-squares' areas add up to the hypotenuse-square's area.

steps.body: That area picture is the proof: for ANY right triangle, the squares built on the two legs have areas a² and b², and together they exactly fill the square built on the hypotenuse, whose area is c². So a² + b² = c² always holds.

explanationVariants: The leg-squares are 6² = 36 and 8² = 64; together c² = 36 + 64 = 100.
Add the squares of the legs: 36 + 64 = 100 = c².

widget.prompt: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. What is c² (the area of the hypotenuse square)?

commonErrors.feedback: That added the legs (6+8), not their squares — c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100.
That multiplied the legs — c² is the SUM of their squares: 36 + 64 = 100.

widget.prompt: In a right triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?

options.label: The side opposite the right angle (the longest side)
options.feedback: Right — the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle and is the longest side.

options.label: The shortest side
options.feedback: The hypotenuse is the LONGEST side, opposite the right angle — not the shortest.

options.label: Either of the two legs
options.feedback: The legs are the two sides FORMING the right angle — the hypotenuse is the third side, opposite it.

options.label: The side along the bottom
options.feedback: Position on the page doesn't matter — the hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle.

explanationVariants: Legs 5 and 12: 25 + 144 = 169, and 13² = 169, so a² + b² = c² checks.

widget.prompt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. What is c² = 5² + 12²?

commonErrors.feedback: That added the legs (5+12), not their squares — 25 + 144 = 169.
That multiplied the legs — c² is 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169.

explanationVariants: The theorem relates the AREAS of squares built on the sides: leg-squares add to the hypotenuse-square.
a², b², c² are the areas of squares on each side; the leg ones sum to the hypotenuse one.

widget.prompt: In a² + b² = c², what do a², b², and c² represent geometrically?

options.label: The areas of squares built on each side
options.feedback: Right — each squared term is the area of the square on that side.

options.label: The lengths of the three sides
options.feedback: The plain letters a, b, c are the lengths — the SQUARES (a², b², c²) are the AREAS.

options.label: The three angles
options.feedback: The theorem is about side lengths and their squares (areas), not angles.

options.label: The perimeter of the triangle
options.feedback: a², b², c² are square AREAS on the sides, not the triangle's perimeter.

explanationVariants: If the leg-squares are 9 and 16, the hypotenuse-square must be 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5.

widget.prompt: The squares on a right triangle's legs have areas 9 and 16. What is the hypotenuse length c?

commonErrors.feedback: That's c² (the area) — the LENGTH c is √25 = 5.
That added the side lengths (3+4) — instead add the AREAS: 9 + 16 = 25, then c = √25 = 5.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The hypotenuse-square area is 9 + 16 = 25, so c = √25 = 5.

hints: The two leg-squares' areas add to the hypotenuse-square's area.

steps.body: The Pythagorean theorem a² + b² = c² is proved by the areas of squares on the sides.
takeaways: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle — the longest side.
The squares on the two legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse.
That area relationship IS a² + b² = c².
steps.teaser: Next: using the theorem to find missing lengths.

concept.body: The Pythagorean theorem a² + b² = c² relates the areas of squares built on a right triangle's sides: the two leg-squares (a², b²) add up to the hypotenuse-square (c²). The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle.

widget.prompt: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. What is c² = 3² + 4²?

commonErrors.feedback: That added the legs (3+4), not their squares — 9 + 16 = 25.
